title: Generic threat catalogue
description: A flat list of threats. Each threat targets one class of the setup ontology; the analysis instantiates it for every matching entity of a plan. A threat only describes the cause and its immediate effect on items; outcomes such as theft or lock-out are computed by checking the spending policies against the affected items. Mitigations are not listed here; mechanisms and recovery actions point to threats.

category_likelihood.description: Base likelihood band (0 to 4, see Ratings.json) of a threat without a `likelihood` of its own, per category. The loader checks that every category has one.

cardinality.description: `set`: the threat involves several entities of the class at once (e.g. people colluding).

subclasses.description: For an abstract class such as Secret: the concrete classes the threat applies to.

source.description: Who or what causes it. `insider` is a person of the plan; `outsider` is anybody else.

phases.description: Lifecycle activities in which the threat can strike.

applies_when.description: The threat is instantiated only on entities for which this holds.

likelihood.description: Base likelihood band (0 to 4, see Ratings.json) before the setup's measures. Without it the category default applies and the line is flagged for review. `ask` marks a value that depends on facts the owner must supply; the answer replaces the value.

likelihood_modifiers.description: Adjustments of the base likelihood for the entities the threat is instantiated on. A modifier that holds for several threats is written in each of them.

target_acts.description: The target persons are themselves the attackers (they act against the setup). What they may do by their access rights is not a failure.

technology.description: Protocol or technology the weakness lies in (protocol-level threats); matched against technology attributes of the plan.

unless.description: Affected items for which this holds are not affected (e.g. a fireproof product in a fire).

only.description: Only affected items for which this holds are affected (e.g. a swapped bag: devices become controlled, backups tampered).
